notes.note: Ambiguity: reading 1 chosen (top-level group identifiers unique among top-level groups); test uses two top-level groups with the same name.
Informative NOTE tested as a reject test with a friend group (8.2.2-014a covers private).
The runs on component type is exercised without importing its name by starting the imported runs-on function on a PTC returned by an imported function (f_create().start(...)).

The runs on component type of the altstep is only exercised indirectly: an imported function running on the unnamed component type invokes the runs-on altstep; the importing module cannot name the component type itself.
Attribute import is observed through an imported template with optional "implicit omit"; encoding-related attributes are not covered.
Imports of the same definition via all, group, kind and single import; checks only that no ambiguity arises (the definition is usable unqualified).
Order of treatment is only weakly observable: an 'all except' import followed by a single import of the excepted definition makes it available.
Ambiguity: literal reading chosen (general rule for connection operations, not limited to imported components).

Ambiguity: 'this rule' read as the name-clash rule. The clashing definition is an integer constant of the importing module (allowed, since clause 6.2.4 restricts names only within the defining module).

Ambiguity: 'this rule' read as the name-clash rule. A clashing definition of the enumerated type itself is avoided (forbidden by example 5); a record constant whose field has the enumerated type is referenced in enumerated context via its qualified name M.e_second.f. Qualified enumerated values (MyEnum.e_second) avoided because Titan does not support them.
